note.explanation: Water and mineral salts enter the root mainly through root hairs. Root hairs take in salts by active transport, and water follows by osmosis. The water and dissolved salts then pass through the root towards the xylem.

Incorrect: the cortex lies just inside the epidermis.
Incorrect: the endodermis forms the innermost boundary of the cortex.

modelAnswer: The epidermis is the outermost covering of the root and is a single layer of cells.
Many epidermal cells have root hairs that extend into the spaces among soil particles; root hairs have a large surface area and are in direct contact with soil water.
Root hairs take in more salts by active transport.
Water moves from soil to root hairs by osmosis because the soil water has a lower concentration of salts than the root hairs.
Water with dissolved salts moves from the root hairs to the other cells of the epidermis, then through the cortex, endodermis and pericycle.
Water from the pericycle moves into the root xylem and is transported to the xylem of the stem.

explain.title: The transport tissues
explain.body: In all land plants except mosses and liverworts, xylem and phloem carry materials. Xylem transports water and salts, while phloem transports food.

explain.title: Passive transport
explain.body: Passive Transport: It is the movement of ions or molecules across cell membrane from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration. This movement does not require energy. Diffusion and osmosis are examples of passive transport.

explain.title: Active transport
explain.body: Active Transport: It is the movement of ions or molecules across cell membrane from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration, using energy. Root hairs take in more salts by active transport.

explain.title: Osmosis
explain.body: Osmosis: It is the movement of water molecules through a semi-permeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration. This movement does not require energy. In the root, water moves from soil into root hairs by osmosis.

explain.title: The route through a root
explain.body: Root hairs take in water and salts from the soil. Water passes through the epidermis and cortex to the endodermis, then to the pericycle and into the xylem.

mistakes: Do not swap the roles of xylem and phloem: xylem transports water and salts; phloem transports food.
Do not say salts enter root hairs by osmosis; the section says salts enter by active transport.
Do not say water enters root hairs by active transport; it enters by osmosis.
Do not leave out the route through cortex, endodermis and pericycle in a long answer.
Do not stop the route at the pericycle; state that water moves into the xylem.
